terms.grammar: adverb, after the word it limits
evidence: Ter. Eun. 638–639: sī illud nōn licet, saltem hoc licēbit
Cic. Att. 9.6.5: ēripe mihi hunc dolōrem aut minue saltem
terms.comment: What still holds when something greater is refused: “if not that, at least this”.

terms.gloss: at least, at any rate; surely
evidence: Phaedr. 4 epil. 7: sī nōn ingenium, certē brevitātem approbā
Quint. 1.1.11: at ūnus certē sit assiduus loquendī nōn imperītus
Varr. RR 2.1.12: minimum octōgintā et ūna (Lewis & Short)

terms.gloss: at any rate, at least; above all
evidence: Cic. Att. 13.48.2: velim M. Varrōnis et Ollī mittās laudātiōnem, Ollī utique
terms.comment: In Cicero mostly in the letters (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: sī illud nōn licet, saltem hoc licēbit
phrases.english: if that isn’t allowed, at least this will be

phrases.latin: ēripe mihi hunc dolōrem aut minue saltem
phrases.english: take this pain away from me, or at least make it less

phrases.latin: sī nōn ingenium, certē brevitātem approbā
phrases.english: if not my talent, at least approve my brevity

sources: Lewis & Short: saltem · Lewis & Short: certe · Lewis & Short: parvus (minimum) · Lewis & Short: utique
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 338.

Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-phaedrus, loci-quintilianus), checked against the editions named there; Terence (Eun. 638–639) and Cicero (Att. 9.6.5, 13.48.2) checked against the Perseus Latin texts.
